clue.text: Vocalist embraces wife, one that's promiscuous

indicators.note: to embrace is to hold in the arms, so the singer's letters wrap round the wife's

explanation.surface: A singer is married, and someone in the picture sleeps around.
explanation.definitionFit: A swinger is slang for a person with a free and easy sex life, especially one who swaps partners.

clue.text: Beetle, for example, not in special group

indicators.note: not means the following word is left out of the other piece

parts.note: a beetle is one kind of insect

explanation.surface: A beetle is excluded from a select club.
explanation.definitionFit: A sect is a small group with distinctive beliefs, set apart from the larger body.

clue.text: A single thing, or a couple

definitions.meaning: one article in a list or collection
two people in a romantic relationship

explanation.surface: One object, or two people: a riddle about number.
explanation.definitionFit: An item is one entry on a list, and two people romantically linked are said to be one.

clue.text: Bloomer that may come to ruin game

indicators.note: the letters may come to form something else once reshuffled

explanation.surface: A blunder could wreck a game.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bloomer' suggests a mistake; here it is a plant that blooms.
explanation.definitionFit: A geranium is a flowering plant, so it is a bloomer in the literal sense.

clue.text: Approximate area of golf course

definitions.meaning: not exact, as in a ballpark estimate
the long grass beside the fairway

explanation.surface: Someone estimates the size of part of a golf course.
explanation.definitionFit: A rough estimate is an approximate one, and the long uncut grass off the fairway has the same name.

clue.text: Friends on TV?

parts.note: Friends was a hugely popular American television comedy series, so it is an example of the genre

explanation.surface: A question about pals appearing on television.
explanation.definitionFit: Friends, the long-running American show, belongs to the genre of situation comedy, so it is one example.

clue.text: Being prepared to receive cash thus in payment?

definitions.meaning: under control, already being dealt with

definitions.text: to receive cash thus in payment?
definitions.meaning: paid directly in notes and coins, often off the books

explanation.surface: Someone stands ready to be paid in cash.
explanation.definitionFit: A task in hand is under control and prepared for; cash paid this way goes straight into the palm.

clue.text: One has no duty to buy this

definitions.text: One has no duty to buy this

parts.words: One has no duty to buy this
parts.note: smuggled goods dodge customs charges, so no tax has been paid on them

explanation.surface: Seems to say nobody is obliged to purchase something.
explanation.walkthrough: 'duty' reads as obligation but means customs tax.
explanation.definitionFit: Contraband is smuggled goods, which have evaded the customs tax normally charged on them.

clue.text: Rename girl Artful Dodger

indicators.note: artful means crafty, so the letters are cunningly rearranged

explanation.surface: An instruction to give a new name to the Artful Dodger, a girl.
explanation.walkthrough: The Artful Dodger is the pickpocket in Dickens's Oliver Twist; the name is split between indicator and definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A malingerer fakes illness to shirk work, so is one who dodges duty.

clue.text: Smack around side of face: buzz off!

indicators.note: the smack's letters go round the outside of the other piece

parts.note: a clout is a hard blow, a smack
an ear sits on the side of the face

explanation.surface: Someone is slapped across the face and told to go away.
explanation.definitionFit: To clear out is an informal command to leave at once, the same as telling someone to get lost.

clue.text: TV station heartless as promoter of beauty products

indicators.note: having no heart means the central letter of the word is dropped

parts.note: a television station is a channel

explanation.surface: A cruel television station is advertising cosmetics.
explanation.walkthrough: 'heartless' removes the middle N of the seven-letter CHANNEL.
explanation.definitionFit: Chanel is the French fashion house famous for perfume and cosmetics, which it markets worldwide.

clue.text: British city shows effect of cuts

parts.note: Leeds is a large city in Yorkshire, northern England

explanation.surface: A city in Britain suffers from spending cuts.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface suggests budget cuts; the definition means cuts to the skin.
explanation.definitionFit: Something that has been cut loses blood, which is the visible result of a wound.

clue.text: Entering the marathon, but not for a while

parts.note: to be entering something is to be in it
a marathon is a long run

explanation.surface: A runner signs up for a marathon but will not be racing soon.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase means eventually, over a long period, so the outcome will not come for some time.

clue.text: Very gloomy summer, a 5

parts.note: black can mean dismal or very gloomy, as in a black mood
a summer here is one who sums, an adder

explanation.surface: A dismal summer season is described.
explanation.walkthrough: 'summer' is the season in the surface; here it is someone who adds up. 'a 5' points to 5-across, SITCOM; Blackadder is a BBC historical comedy series starring Rowan Atkinson.
explanation.definitionFit: Blackadder is a classic British situation comedy, so it is an example of the type named at 5.

clue.text: I try weapon out: there's no going back from this

definitions.text: there's no going back from this

indicators.note: out suggests the letters are thrown out of order

explanation.surface: Someone tests a weapon, knowing it cannot be undone.
explanation.definitionFit: A journey with no return leg is one where the traveller does not come back.

clue.text: Left in agony, went into decline

explanation.surface: A sufferer was abandoned in pain and deteriorated.
explanation.definitionFit: To languish is to weaken or waste away, so the past tense describes going downhill.

clue.text: Small photo of race

parts.note: a print is a photograph developed on paper

explanation.surface: A little snapshot taken at a race.
explanation.definitionFit: A sprint is a short race run at full speed.

clue.text: Short alert from pager or buzzer

indicators.note: short means cut off at the end, so the final letter goes

parts.note: a pager signals with a beep

explanation.surface: A pager or a doorbell gives a brief warning sound.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Short' drops the last letter, P, from BEEP. 'buzzer' looks like part of the device list but is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A bee is an insect that buzzes as it flies, so it is a buzzer in a playful sense.

clue.text: Hit man who can't afford his own weapon?

definitions.text: Hit man who can't afford his own weapon?

parts.words: Hit man who can't afford his own weapon?
parts.note: a contract killer, jokingly pictured as one who must rent his pistol

explanation.surface: A broke assassin has to rent a gun.
explanation.definitionFit: A professional killer paid for a job is called this, read whimsically as a gunman whose firearm is rented.

clue.text: Intimidate Daisy?

definitions.meaning: Daisy is a traditional name for a dairy animal in children's stories

explanation.surface: Someone is bullying a girl called Daisy.
explanation.definitionFit: To cow is to browbeat; and a stereotypical name for a milking animal is Daisy, so it is an example.

clue.text: Foreknowledge of screen epic to be redistributed

indicators.note: redistributing the letters spreads them into a new order

explanation.surface: Knowing in advance that a film epic will get a wider release.
explanation.definitionFit: Prescience is knowledge of events before they happen, a synonym for foresight.

clue.text: Clever idea asthmatic has

definitions.meaning: a crafty scheme or trick, in British slang
a whistling breath that a person with asthma suffers

explanation.surface: Someone with asthma has a bright idea.
explanation.definitionFit: In British slang a cunning plan is this, and the word is also the rasping breath of asthma.

clue.text: Porter's work that doesn't follow the rules?

definitions.meaning: a 1934 musical by the American songwriter Cole Porter
a situation where no rules apply and everything is permitted

explanation.surface: A doorman's job seems to break every rule.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Porter' looks like a hotel or railway porter; it is Cole Porter, the American composer.
explanation.definitionFit: Cole Porter wrote the musical of that title, and the phrase also describes a state with no restrictions at all.

clue.text: A lot of money? Splendid!

definitions.meaning: slang for a thousand pounds or dollars
an exclamation meaning excellent or great

explanation.surface: Someone is delighted at a large sum.
explanation.definitionFit: Slang for a thousand pounds or dollars, and an exclamation of approval meaning great.

clue.text: They may go spare in your Chinese meal

definitions.text: They may go spare in your Chinese meal

parts.words: They may go spare in your Chinese meal
parts.note: go spare also means become very angry

explanation.surface: Diners lose their temper over a Chinese meal.
explanation.walkthrough: 'go spare' is British slang for becoming furious; here it attaches 'spare' to the answer to name a dish.
explanation.definitionFit: Pork spare ribs are a staple of Chinese restaurant menus, so the bones are in the meal.

clue.text: Like an omelette? For starters, extremely good Greek yoghurt

indicators.note: starters are the opening letters of each of the following words

explanation.surface: A menu note: an omelette, with Greek yoghurt to begin.
explanation.definitionFit: An omelette is made from beaten eggs, so it tastes or looks of them.

clue.text: Strode around the county

indicators.note: turning the letters around puts them into a fresh order

explanation.surface: Someone walked about the English countryside.
explanation.definitionFit: Dorset is a county on the south coast of England, so it is an example.

clue.text: Tall and skinny, first to go fishing

indicators.note: only the first letter of the following word is wanted

parts.note: angling is fishing with rod and line

explanation.surface: A lanky person is the first to set off fishing.
explanation.definitionFit: Gangling describes someone tall, thin and awkward in movement, a synonym for lanky.

clue.text: One knocking a recording artist

definitions.meaning: someone who raps on a door
a musician who performs rap music

explanation.surface: Someone at the door turns out to be a musician.
explanation.definitionFit: One who raps on a door knocks; a rap musician makes records.

clue.text: Soap with unpleasant conclusion

parts.note: an American television soap opera whose name finishes with a word meaning unpleasant

explanation.surface: A television soap opera ends badly.
explanation.walkthrough: The 'unpleasant conclusion' is the last five letters of the title, which spell a word for horrid.
explanation.definitionFit: Dynasty was a 1980s American soap opera about a rich oil family, and its title ends in a word meaning mean or vile.
